sentences.zh: 【梁紀十】　上章閹茂，一年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 10] Above: Zhang Yanyan; one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 10] The cycle opens with Zhang Yanyan; one year.

translations.literal: The tenth year of Emperor Wu of Liang, Zhongdatong 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, year ten of Zhongdatong (

translations.idiomatic: gengxu, 530 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑，魏益州刺史長孫壽、梁州刺史元俊等遣將擊嚴始欣，斬之，蕭玩等亦敗死，失亡萬餘人。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day jichou, Wei's Inspector of Yizhou Changsun Shou, Inspector of Liangzhou Yuan Jun, and others sent generals to attack Yan Shixin, beheaded him; Xiao Wan and others were also defeated and died, with more than ten thousand lost.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jichou, Wei's Yizhou inspector Changsun Shou, Liangzhou inspector Yuan Jun, and others sent generals against Yan Shixin and beheaded him. Xiao Wan and others were likewise defeated and killed; losses exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏東徐州城民呂文欣等殺刺史元大賓，據城反，魏遣都官尚書平城樊子鵠等討之。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the people of Wei's Eastern Xuzhou city, Lü Wenxin and others, killed the inspector Yuan Dabin, seized the city, and rebelled. Wei sent the Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Pingcheng, Fan Zihu, and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the townsfolk of Wei's Eastern Xuzhou—Lü Wenxin and his fellows—murdered Inspector Yuan Dabin, held the city, and rose in revolt. Wei dispatched Fan Zihu of Pingcheng, director of the imperial secretariat, and others to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，斬文欣。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day jiayin, Wenxin was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, Wenxin was executed.

sentences.zh: -{万俟}-丑奴侵擾關中，魏爾朱榮遣武衛將軍賀拔岳討之。

translations.literal: Moqi Chounu harassed Guanzhong. Wei's Erzhu Rong sent the Martial Guards General Heba Yue to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu raided Guanzhong. Erzhu Rong of Wei sent Martial Guards General Heba Yue against him.

sentences.zh: 岳私謂其兄勝曰：「丑奴，勍敵也。

translations.literal: Yue privately told his elder brother Sheng, "Chounu is a powerful foe.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said privately to his elder brother Sheng, "Chounu is a formidable enemy.

sentences.zh: 今攻之不勝，固有罪；

translations.literal: If we attack now and do not win, guilt is certain;
translations.idiomatic: If we attack and fail, we are surely guilty;

sentences.zh: 勝之，讒嫉將生。

translations.literal: if we win, slander and envy will arise.
translations.idiomatic: if we win, slander and envy will follow.

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「然則奈何？

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Then what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng asked, "Then what should we do?

sentences.zh: 」岳曰：「願得爾朱氏一人為帥而佐之。

translations.literal: " Yue said, "I wish to have one of the Erzhu clan as commander while I assist him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said, "Let one of the Erzhu house lead, with me as his lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 」勝為之言於榮，榮悅，以爾朱天光為使持節、都督二雍、二岐諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、雍州刺史，以岳為左大都督，又以征西將軍代郡侯莫陳悅為右大都督，並為天光之副以討之。

translations.literal: " Sheng spoke for him to Rong. Rong was pleased and made Erzhu Tianguang Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Two Yong and Two Qi military affairs, Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Inspector of Yongzhou; made Yue Left Grand Commander; and also made the Campaigning Western General, Houmochen Yue of Dai commandery, Right Grand Commander—all as Tianguang's deputies for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng pleaded his case to Rong. Rong was pleased. He appointed Erzhu Tianguang bearer of the staff, commander of the Two Yong and Two Qi theaters, Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Yongzhou inspector; Heba Yue as left grand commander; and Campaigning Western General Houmochen Yue of Dai as right grand commander—all serving under Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光初行，唯配軍士千人，發洛陽以西路次民馬以給之。

translations.literal: When Tianguang first set out, he was allotted only a thousand soldiers. Leaving Luoyang, he was to requisition horses from the people along the western route to supply his force.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang set out with only a thousand men assigned him. From Luoyang he was to levy horses from households along the western road.

sentences.zh: 時赤水蜀賊斷路，詔侍中楊侃先行慰諭，並稅其馬，蜀持疑不下。

translations.literal: At that time Shu bandits at Chishui blocked the road. An edict ordered Palace Attendant Yang Kan to go ahead to reassure them and levy their horses as well. The Shu held back in doubt and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu raiders at Chishui were blocking the road. The court ordered Palace Attendant Yang Kan ahead to reassure them and levy their horses too. The Shu hesitated and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 軍至潼關，天光不敢進，岳曰：「蜀賊鼠竊，公尚遲疑，若遇大敵，將何以戰！

translations.literal: When the army reached Tong Pass, Tianguang dared not advance. Yue said, "Shu bandits are rats at thievery—yet you still hesitate. If we met a great enemy, how would we fight!
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass Tianguang would not advance. Yue said, "These Shu thieves are mere pillagers, and you still hesitate. Facing a real foe, how would we fight?

sentences.zh: 」天光曰：「今日之事，一以相委。

translations.literal: " Tianguang said, "Today's affair I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianguang said, "Today's business is entirely yours.

sentences.zh: 」岳遂進擊蜀於渭北，破之，獲馬二千匹。

translations.literal: " Yue then advanced and struck the Shu on the north bank of the Wei, defeated them, and captured two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue marched north of the Wei, routed the Shu, and took two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 簡其壯健以充軍士，又稅民馬合萬餘匹。

translations.literal: He selected the strong and healthy to fill out the ranks and levied civilian horses as well, totaling more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the sturdiest into the ranks and levied civilian mounts until he had more than ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 以軍士尚少，淹留未進。

translations.literal: Because the soldiers were still few, he halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Still short of troops, he halted and did not press on.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，遣騎兵參軍劉貴乘驛至軍中責天光，杖之一百，以軍士二千人益之。

translations.literal: Rong was angry and sent Cavalry Adjutant Liu Gui by post-horse to the army to rebuke Tianguang and cane him a hundred strokes, adding two thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, furious, sent Cavalry Adjutant Liu Gui by relay horse to rebuke Tianguang, give him a hundred strokes of the cane, and reinforce him with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 三月，丑奴自將其眾圍岐州，遣其大行台尉遲菩薩、僕射-{万俟}-仵自武功南渡渭，攻圍趣柵。

translations.literal: In the third month, Chounu personally led his host to besiege Qizhou and sent his Grand Commissioner Yuchi Pusa and Vice Director Moqi Wu from Wugong south across the Wei to attack and surround the stockade at Qu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Chounu himself besieged Qizhou. He sent Grand Commissioner Yuchi Pusa and Vice Director Moqi Wu from Wugong to cross the Wei southward and invest the stockade at Qu.

sentences.zh: 天光使賀拔岳將千騎救之。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent Heba Yue with a thousand horse to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent Heba Yue with a thousand cavalry to relieve the place.

sentences.zh: 菩薩等已拔柵而還，岳故殺掠其吏民以挑之，菩薩帥步騎二萬至渭北。

translations.literal: Pusa and the others had already taken the stockade and withdrawn. Yue deliberately killed and plundered their officials and people to provoke them. Pusa led twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa had already stormed the stockade and withdrawn. Yue deliberately slaughtered and plundered civilians to bait them. Pusa marched twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 岳以輕騎數十自渭南與菩薩隔水而語，稱揚國威，菩薩令省事傳語，岳怒曰：「我與菩薩語，卿何人也！

translations.literal: Yue took several dozen light horse from south of Weinan and spoke with Pusa across the water, proclaiming the state's majesty. Pusa had a clerk relay words. Yue raged: "I speak with Pusa—who are you!
translations.idiomatic: Yue led several dozen light horsemen from south of Weinan and hailed Pusa across the river, vaunting the empire's might. Pusa sent a clerk to answer. Yue thundered, "I address Pusa—who are you?

sentences.zh: 」射殺之。

translations.literal: " and shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: " and shot him down.

sentences.zh: 明日，復引百餘騎隔水與賊語，稍引而東，至水淺可涉之處，岳即馳馬東出。

translations.literal: The next day he again led a hundred-odd horse to speak with the bandits across the water, drawing them gradually east to where the water was shallow enough to ford; then Yue spurred east at a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he brought a hundred-odd horsemen to parley across the water again, edging eastward to a shallow ford—then wheeled and galloped east.

sentences.zh: 賊以為走，乃棄步兵，輕騎南渡渭追岳。

translations.literal: The bandits thought he was fleeing, abandoned their infantry, and with light horse crossed the Wei southward in pursuit of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought he fled. They left their foot soldiers, crossed the Wei with light cavalry, and chased Yue.

sentences.zh: 岳依橫岡設伏兵以待之，賊半渡岡東，岳還兵擊之，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Yue, relying on a transverse ridge, set ambush to await them. When half the bandits had crossed the ridge eastward, Yue turned his troops and struck; the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yue laid ambush along a lateral ridge. When half the enemy had crossed eastward, he wheeled and struck; they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 岳下令，賊下馬者勿殺；

translations.literal: Yue gave the order: do not kill those who dismount;
translations.idiomatic: Yue ordered: spare any man who dismounts;

sentences.zh: 賊悉投馬，俄獲三千人，馬亦無遺，遂擒菩薩。

translations.literal: the bandits all cast off their horses. In no time three thousand men were taken, not a horse lost, and Pusa was captured.
translations.idiomatic: they all threw down their horses. Within moments he had three thousand men and every horse, and took Pusa alive.

sentences.zh: 仍渡渭北，降步卒萬餘，並收其輜重。

translations.literal: He then crossed to the north bank of the Wei, received the surrender of more than ten thousand foot soldiers, and seized their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed to the north bank, accepted the surrender of ten thousand foot soldiers, and seized their baggage.

sentences.zh: 丑奴聞之，棄岐州，北走安定，置柵於平亭。

translations.literal: When Chounu heard of it, he abandoned Qizhou, fled north to Anding, and built a stockade at Pingting.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu, hearing this, abandoned Qizhou, fled north to Anding, and fortified Pingting.

sentences.zh: 天光方自雍至岐，與岳合。

translations.literal: Tianguang had just come from Yong to Qi and joined Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang had just arrived from Yong at Qi and united with Yue.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，天光至汧、渭之間，停軍牧馬，宣言：「天時將熱，未可行師，俟秋涼更圖進止。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Tianguang reached the region between Qian and Wei, halted the army to pasture horses, and proclaimed: "The season will soon grow hot; we cannot march yet. Wait until autumn cools, then decide advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Tianguang reached the Qian–Wei country, camped to graze his horses, and announced: "Heat is coming—we cannot march yet. We will decide in the cool of autumn.

sentences.zh: 」獲丑奴覘候者，縱遣之。

translations.literal: " They captured Chounu's scouts and set them free.
translations.idiomatic: " They took Chounu's scouts and let them go.

sentences.zh: 丑奴信之，散眾耕於細川，使其太尉侯伏侯元進將兵五千，據險立柵，其餘千人已下為柵者甚眾。

translations.literal: Chounu believed it, dispersed his host to farm in Xichuan, and had his Grand Marshal Houfu Hou Yuanjin lead five thousand men to hold the heights and build a stockade; very many stockades were built with a thousand men or fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu believed them, scattered his men to farm in Xichuan, and posted Grand Marshal Houfu Hou Yuanjin with five thousand on the heights behind palisades; countless smaller camps held a thousand men or fewer.

sentences.zh: 天光知其勢分，晡時，密嚴諸軍，相繼俱發。

translations.literal: Tianguang knew their strength was divided. In the late afternoon he secretly arrayed the armies and sent them out one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang saw their force was divided. Toward dusk he quietly mustered the host and sent column after column forward.

sentences.zh: 黎明，圍元進大柵，拔之。

translations.literal: At dawn they surrounded Yuanjin's great stockade and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they invested Yuanjin's main camp and stormed it.

sentences.zh: 所得俘囚，一皆縱遣，諸柵聞之皆降。

translations.literal: All captives taken were released. Hearing of it, every stockade surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Every captive was released. At the news, the rest of the camps surrendered.

sentences.zh: 天光晝夜徑進，抵安定城下，賊涇州刺史侯幾長貴以城降。

translations.literal: Tianguang pressed on day and night straight to Anding city. The bandits' Jingzhou inspector Houji Changgui surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang drove day and night to Anding. The rebels' Jingzhou inspector Houji Changgui yielded the city.

sentences.zh: 丑奴棄平亭走，欲趣高平，天光遣賀拔岳輕騎追之，丁卯，及於平涼。

translations.literal: Chounu abandoned Pingting and fled, intending to make for Gaoping. Tianguang sent Heba Yue with light horse in pursuit; on day dingmao he caught up at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu abandoned Pingting and ran for Gaoping. Tianguang sent Heba Yue in light pursuit; on dingmao he overtook him at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 賊未成列，直閣代郡侯莫陳崇單騎入賊中，於馬上生擒丑奴，因大呼，眾皆披靡，無敢當者，後騎益集，賊眾崩潰，遂大破之。

translations.literal: The bandits had not yet formed ranks when Palace Attendant Houmochen Chong of Dai commandery rode alone into their midst, seized Chounu alive from his saddle, and shouted. All crumpled; none dared stand against him. More horse gathered from the rear; the rebel host collapsed and was utterly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rebels could form line, Palace Attendant Houmochen Chong of Dai rode alone into their ranks, snatched Chounu alive from the saddle, and roared. The host buckled; none dared meet him. Reinforcements poured in; the enemy shattered completely.

sentences.zh: 天光進逼高平，城中執送蕭寶寅以降。

translations.literal: Tianguang pressed on Gaoping. The city bound and sent Xiao Baoyin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang advanced on Gaoping. The city seized Xiao Baoyin and surrendered him.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以吐谷渾王佛輔為西秦、河二州刺史。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the Tuyuhun king Fofu was made Inspector of the two provinces of Western Qin and He.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Tuyuhun King Fofu was appointed inspector of Western Qin and He provinces.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏以關中平，大赦。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, because Guanzhong was pacified, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, with Guanzhong pacified, Wei declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: -{万俟}-丑奴、蕭寶寅至洛陽，置閶闔門外都街之中，士女聚觀凡三日。

translations.literal: Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin reached Luoyang and were placed in the broad avenue outside the Changhe Gate. Men and women gathered to watch for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin were brought to Luoyang and displayed in the main avenue outside Changhe Gate. Crowds of men and women watched for three days.

sentences.zh: 丹楊王蕭贊表請寶寅之命，吏部尚書李神俊、黃門侍郎高道穆素與寶寅善，欲左右之，言於魏主曰：「寶寅叛逆，事在前朝。

translations.literal: Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan memorialized asking Baoyin's life. Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenjun and Yellow Gate Attendant Gao Daomu had long been friendly with Baoyin and wished to sway the decision. They said to the Wei sovereign, "Baoyin's rebellion belongs to the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan petitioned for Baoyin's life. Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun and Yellow Gate Attendant Gao Daomu, who had long been close to Baoyin, sought to sway the court. They told the Wei emperor, "Baoyin's treason belongs to the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 」會應詔王道習自外至，帝問道習在外所聞，對曰：「唯聞李尚書、高黃門與蕭寶寅周款，並居得言之地，必能全之。

translations.literal: " At that time Rescript Attendant Wang Daoxi arrived from outside. The Emperor asked what Daoxi had heard abroad. He answered: "I have only heard that Minister Li and Attendant Gao are on intimate terms with Xiao Baoyin, and both stand where they can speak freely—they will surely save him.
translations.idiomatic: " Rescript Attendant Wang Daoxi had just arrived from the provinces. The emperor asked what he had heard abroad. He replied, "I hear only that Minister Li and Attendant Gao are intimate with Xiao Baoyin and sit where their words carry weight—they will surely save him.

sentences.zh: 且二人謂寶寅叛逆在前朝，寶寅為丑奴太傅，豈非陛下時邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, the two say Baoyin's rebellion was in the previous reign—but was not Baoyin Grand Tutor to Chounu in Your Majesty's time?
translations.idiomatic: And when they say his treason was 'in the previous reign,' was he not Chounu's Grand Tutor under Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 賊臣不剪，法欲安施！

translations.literal: If traitors are not cut down, how can law be applied!
translations.idiomatic: If traitors go unpunished, what becomes of the law?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃賜寶寅死於駝牛署，斬丑奴於都市。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then had Baoyin put to death at the Camel-Ox Office and Chounu beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then had Baoyin executed at the Camel-Ox Office and Chounu beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，帝復以魏汝南王悅為魏王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day dingsi, the Emperor again made Wei's Prince of Runan, Yue, Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the emperor restored Wei's Prince of Runan, Yue, as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏詔胡氏親屬受爵於朝者皆黜為民。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Wei ordered that all kinsmen of the Hu clan who had received noble ranks at court be degraded to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wei decreed that every Hu clansman who had taken a court noble rank be reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以魏降將范遵為安北將軍、司州牧，從魏王悅北還。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, the surrendered Wei general Fan Zun was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sizhou, to return north with Prince of Wei Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Wei defector Fan Zun was made General Who Pacifies the North and Sizhou governor, to accompany Prince of Wei Yue north.

sentences.zh: -{万俟}-丑奴既敗，自涇、豳以西至靈州，賊黨皆降於魏，唯所署行台-{万俟}-道洛帥眾六千逃入山中，不降。

translations.literal: After Moqi Chounu's defeat, from Jing and Bin west to Lingzhou, the rebel factions all surrendered to Wei—only the Grand Commissioner he had appointed, Moqi Daoluo, led six thousand men into the mountains and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Moqi Chounu's defeat, rebel bands from Jing and Bin west to Lingzhou all surrendered to Wei—save the grand commissioner Chounu had appointed, Moqi Daoluo, who led six thousand into the hills and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 時高平大旱，爾朱天光以馬乏草，退屯城東五十里，遣都督長孫邪利帥二百人行原州事以鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time Gaoping suffered great drought. Erzhu Tianguang, his horses lacking fodder, withdrew to camp fifty li east of the city and sent Commander-in-Chief Changsun Xieli with two hundred men to administer Yuanzhou affairs and hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping was in severe drought. Tianguang, short of forage, fell back fifty li east of the city and sent Commander Changsun Xieli with two hundred men to govern Yuanzhou and hold the town.

sentences.zh: 道洛潛與城民通謀，掩襲邪利，並其所部皆殺之。

translations.literal: Daoluo secretly plotted with the townspeople, made a surprise attack on Xieli, and killed him and all his men.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo conspired with the townsfolk, struck Xieli by surprise, and killed him and his entire command.

sentences.zh: 天光帥諸軍赴之，道洛出戰而敗，帥其眾西入牽屯山，據險自守。

translations.literal: Tianguang led the armies to the rescue. Daoluo came out to fight and was defeated, then led his host west into Qiantun Mountain and held the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang marched to the rescue. Daoluo gave battle, lost, and withdrew west into Qiantun Mountain to hold the passes.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮以天光失邪利，不獲道洛，復遣使杖之一百。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, because Tianguang had lost Xieli and failed to take Daoluo, again sent an envoy to cane him a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, angry that Tianguang had lost Xieli and let Daoluo escape, again sent an envoy to cane him a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 以詔書黜天光為撫軍將軍、雍州刺史，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: By imperial edict Tianguang was demoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, and his noble rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Tianguang to General Who Pacifies the Army and Yongzhou inspector, and lowered his noble rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 天光追擊道洛於牽屯，道洛敗走，入隴，歸略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Tianguang pursued Daoluo at Qiantun. Daoluo was defeated and fled, entered Long, and joined the Lüeyang bandit chief Wang Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang pursued Daoluo at Qiantun. Daoluo was beaten, fled into Long, and joined the Lüeyang rebel Wang Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 道洛驍果絕倫，慶雲得之，甚喜，謂大事可濟，遂稱帝於水洛城，置百官，以道洛為大將軍。

translations.literal: Daoluo's valor was unmatched. Qingyun, gaining him, was greatly pleased and said great things could be achieved. He thereupon declared himself emperor at Shuiluo city, set up the full bureaucracy, and made Daoluo Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo's fighting spirit was unrivaled. Qingyun, delighted to have him, declared that the cause could yet succeed. He proclaimed himself emperor at Shuiluo, installed a full court, and made Daoluo grand general.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，天光帥諸軍入隴，至水洛城，慶雲、道洛出戰，天光射道洛中臂，失弓還走，拔其東城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Tianguang led the armies into Long to Shuiluo city. Qingyun and Daoluo came out to fight. Tianguang shot Daoluo in the arm; he dropped his bow and fled. Tianguang took the eastern wall of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Tianguang entered Long and reached Shuiluo. Qingyun and Daoluo marched out. Tianguang wounded Daoluo's arm with an arrow; he dropped his bow and ran. Tianguang stormed the eastern quarter of the city.

sentences.zh: 賊並兵趣西城，城中無水，眾渴乏，有降者言慶雲、道洛欲突走。

translations.literal: The bandits massed at the western wall. The city had no water; the host was parched with thirst. A defector said Qingyun and Daoluo meant to break out.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed on the western wall. The city had no water; the garrison was desperate with thirst. A man who surrendered said Qingyun and Daoluo planned a breakout.

sentences.zh: 天光恐失之，乃遣人招諭慶雲使早降，曰：「若未能自決，當聽諸人今夜共議，明晨早報。

translations.literal: Tianguang, fearing to lose them, sent men to summon Qingyun to surrender early, saying: "If you cannot decide for yourselves, let your people deliberate tonight and report at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would escape, Tianguang sent envoys urging Qingyun to surrender soon, saying, "If you cannot decide alone, let your men counsel tonight and answer at dawn.

sentences.zh: 」慶雲等冀得少緩，因待夜突出，乃報曰：「請俟明日。

translations.literal: " Qingyun and the others hoped for a little respite; planning a night breakout, they replied: "Please wait until tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingyun and his fellows wanted breathing room—they meant to burst out by night—and answered, "Grant us until tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」天光因使謂曰：「知須水，今相為小退，任取澗水飲之。

translations.literal: " Tianguang then sent word: "I know you need water. We shall draw back a little; take what you need from the stream.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianguang then said, "I know you lack water. We will pull back a little; drink from the brook as you please.

sentences.zh: 」賊眾悅，無復走心。

translations.literal: " The rebel host was pleased and no longer thought of flight.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels rejoiced and lost all thought of escape.

sentences.zh: 天光密使軍士多作木槍，各長七尺，昏後，繞城布列，要路加厚。

translations.literal: Tianguang secretly had the soldiers make many wooden pikes, each seven feet long. After dusk they ringed the city; the main roads were doubled in thickness.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang secretly ordered thousands of wooden pikes, each seven feet long. After dark they ringed the walls, packing the choke points twice as thick.

sentences.zh: 又伏人槍中，備其衝突，兼令密縛長梯於城北。

translations.literal: He also hid men among the pikes to guard against a rush, and had long ladders bound in secret at the north wall.
translations.idiomatic: Men lay hidden among the pikes to block a charge, and long ladders were lashed in secret at the north wall.

sentences.zh: 其夜，慶雲、道洛果馳馬突出，遇槍，馬各傷倒，伏兵起，即時擒之。

translations.literal: That night Qingyun and Daoluo indeed spurred out. They met the pikes; the horses were all wounded and fell. The ambush rose and seized them at once.
translations.idiomatic: That night Qingyun and Daoluo galloped out—and met the pikes. Horses went down screaming. Ambushers sprang up and took them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 軍士緣梯入城，餘眾皆出城南，遇槍而止，窮窘乞降。

translations.literal: Soldiers climbed the ladders into the city. The rest all rushed out the south gate, were stopped by the pikes, and in extremity begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers scaled the ladders into the city. The remainder poured south, were halted by the pikes, and in desperation surrendered.

sentences.zh: 丙子，天光悉收其仗而坑之，死者萬七千人，分其家口。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Tianguang collected all their weapons and buried them alive—seventeen thousand dead—and distributed their households.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Tianguang disarmed them all and buried them alive—seventeen thousand dead—and parceled out their families.

sentences.zh: 於是三秦、河、渭、瓜、涼、鄯州皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the provinces of Sanqin, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Then Sanqin, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan provinces all submitted.

sentences.zh: 天光頓軍略陽。

translations.literal: Tianguang encamped at Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang camped at Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 詔復天光官爵，尋加侍中、儀同三司。

translations.literal: An edict restored Tianguang's office and rank; soon he was further made Palace Attendant and Holder of the Same Rank as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Tianguang's offices and titles; soon he was also made palace attendant with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 以賀拔岳為涇州刺史，侯莫陳悅為渭州刺史。

translations.literal: Heba Yue was made Inspector of Jingzhou; Houmochen Yue was made Inspector of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue became Jingzhou inspector; Houmochen Yue became Weizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 秦州城民謀殺刺史駱超，南秦州城民謀殺刺史辛顯，超、顯皆覺之，走歸天光，天光遣兵討平之。

translations.literal: The people of Qinzhou city plotted to kill Inspector Luo Chao; the people of Southern Qinzhou city plotted to kill Inspector Xin Xian. Chao and Xian both discovered it, fled to Tianguang, and Tianguang sent troops to pacify the plots.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou townsfolk plotted to murder Inspector Luo Chao; Southern Qinzhou townsfolk plotted against Inspector Xin Xian. Both men discovered the plots, fled to Tianguang, and he sent troops to crush the conspiracies.

sentences.zh: 步兵校尉宇文泰從賀拔岳入關，以功遷征西將軍，行原州事。

translations.literal: Footsoldiers Commandant Yuwen Tai followed Heba Yue into the passes. For merit he was promoted to Campaigning Western General and Acting Administrator of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Footsoldiers Commandant Yuwen Tai followed Heba Yue into Guanzhong. For his service he was promoted to Campaigning Western General and acting administrator of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時關、隴凋弊，泰撫以恩信，民皆感悅，曰：「早遇宇文使君，吾輩豈從亂乎！

translations.literal: At that time Guan and Long were wasted and impoverished. Tai governed with kindness and trust; the people were all moved and said, "Had we met Commissioner Yuwen earlier, how could we have followed rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Long were ravaged and poor. Tai ruled with kindness and good faith; the people said with feeling, "Had we met Commissioner Yuwen sooner, how could we have gone to war?

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，上餞魏王悅於德陽堂，遣兵送至境上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day gengxu, the Emperor feasted Prince of Wei Yue at Deyang Hall and sent troops to escort him to the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengxu, the emperor gave a farewell feast for Prince of Wei Yue at Deyang Hall and sent troops to escort him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 魏爾朱榮雖居外籓，遙制朝政，樹置親黨，布列魏主左右，伺察動靜，大小必知。

translations.literal: Wei's Erzhu Rong, though he dwelt in an outer fief, controlled court affairs from afar, planted his kin, and stationed them about the Wei sovereign's person to watch every movement; great and small, nothing escaped him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong of Wei, though he held his domains abroad, steered the court from a distance, planted his kin, and posted them around the emperor to watch his every move—nothing large or small escaped him.

sentences.zh: 魏主雖受制於榮，然性勤政事，朝夕不倦，數親覽辭訟，理冤獄。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign, though constrained by Rong, was by nature diligent in government, tireless morning and evening, often personally hearing lawsuits and righting wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor, though Rong's prisoner in all but name, was by nature diligent—he toiled from dawn to dusk, often heard cases himself, and cleared wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of it, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Rong heard of it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝又與吏部尚書李神俊議清治選部，榮嘗關補曲陽縣令，神俊以階懸，不奏，別更擬人。

translations.literal: The Emperor also discussed with Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun cleansing and reforming the selection bureau. Rong had once intervened to appoint the magistrate of Quyang county. Shenjun, because the rank was too high, did not memorialize it and nominated another man instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also discussed with Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun reforming the Board of Selection. Rong had once pushed through an appointment as magistrate of Quyang. Shenjun, finding the rank inappropriate, did not memorialize it and proposed another candidate.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，即遣所補者往奪其任。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly angered and immediately sent the man he had appointed to seize the post.
translations.idiomatic: Rong flew into a rage and sent his nominee at once to take the post by force.

sentences.zh: 神俊懼而辭位，榮使尚書左僕射爾朱世隆攝選。

translations.literal: Shenjun, in fear, resigned his office. Rong had Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Erzhu Shilong act as selection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun, terrified, resigned. Rong had Left Vice Director Erzhu Shilong take charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 榮啟北人為河南諸州，帝未之許；

translations.literal: Rong memorialized to place northerners in the Henan provinces. The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Rong petitioned to install northerners as governors across the Henan provinces. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 太宰天穆入見面論，帝猶不許。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Tianmu came in audience to argue face to face. The Emperor still would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Tianmu came to argue in person. The emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 天穆曰：「天柱既有大功，為國宰相，若請普代天下官，恐陛下亦不得違之，如何啟數人為州，遽不用也！

translations.literal: Tianmu said, "Heaven's Pillar has such great merit and is the state's chief minister. If he asked to replace all officers under heaven, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either—so why petition for only a few men as provincial governors and reject it at once!
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu said, "Heaven's Pillar has earned such merit and is chief minister of the realm. If he asked to replace every officer in the empire, Your Majesty could hardly refuse—so why refuse a mere handful of provincial posts!

sentences.zh: 」帝正色曰：「天柱若不為人臣，朕亦須代；

translations.literal: " The Emperor said sternly, "If Heaven's Pillar will not be a subject, I too must be replaced;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said coldly, "If Heaven's Pillar will not be a subject, then replace me too;

sentences.zh: 如其猶存臣節，無代天下百官之理！

translations.literal: but if he still keeps the deportment of a subject, there is no reason to replace all officers under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: but so long as he keeps the deportment of a subject, he has no claim to replace every officer in the empire!

sentences.zh: 」榮聞之，大恚恨，曰：「天子由誰得立！

translations.literal: " When Rong heard of it, he was greatly resentful and said, "By whom did the Son of Heaven gain the throne!
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong heard this, he burned with resentment. "Who put the Son of Heaven on the throne?

sentences.zh: 今乃不用我語！

translations.literal: And now he will not use my words!
translations.idiomatic: And now he will not heed me!

sentences.zh: 爾朱皇后性□石忌，屢致忿恚。

translations.literal: Empress Erzhu was by nature fiercely jealous, repeatedly provoking rage.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Erzhu was fiercely jealous by nature and provoked quarrels again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝遣爾朱世隆語以大理，後曰：「天子由我家置立，今便如此；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Erzhu Shilong to speak to her of reason. The empress said, "The Son of Heaven was set on the throne by our house—yet now he acts thus;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Erzhu Shilong to reason with her. The empress said, "Our house set the Son of Heaven on the throne—and this is how he repays us?

sentences.zh: 我父本即自作，今亦復決。

translations.literal: My father was ready to act for himself from the first; now he has decided again.
translations.idiomatic: My father could have taken the throne himself to begin with—and now he has made up his mind again.

sentences.zh: 」世隆曰：「止自不為，若本自為之，臣今亦封王矣。

translations.literal: Shilong said, "He simply chose not to. Had he acted for himself from the first, your servant would by now be enfeoffed as a king.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "He simply chose not to. Had he acted for himself from the start, I would be a king by now.

sentences.zh: 帝既外逼於榮，內迫皇后，恆怏怏不以萬乘為樂，唯幸寇盜未息，欲使與榮相持。

translations.literal: The Emperor, pressed from without by Rong and from within by the empress, was constantly discontent and took no joy in the imperial throne; he only hoped the bandits would not be pacified, so that Rong might be kept occupied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, harried from without by Rong and from within by the empress, found no joy in the throne; he could only hope the rebels would not be crushed, so Rong might stay busy.

sentences.zh: 及關、隴既定，告捷之日，乃不甚喜，謂尚書令臨淮王彧曰：「即今天下便是無賊。

translations.literal: When Guan and Long were settled and the day of victory reports came, he was not greatly pleased. He said to Minister of the Left and Prince of Linhuai Yu, "From this day the empire has no rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan and Long were pacified and the victory dispatches arrived, he was scarcely pleased. He told Minister of the Left and Prince of Linhuai Yu, "As of today the realm has no more bandits.

sentences.zh: 」彧見帝色不悅，曰：「臣恐賊平之後，方勞聖慮。

translations.literal: Yu, seeing the emperor's displeased look, said, "Your servant fears that after the rebels are pacified, Your Majesty's cares will only begin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, reading the emperor's face, said, "I fear that once the bandits are gone, Your Majesty's true troubles will begin.

sentences.zh: 」帝畏餘人怪之，還以它語亂之曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing others would think it strange, turned aside with other words: "Indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid others would notice, the emperor changed the subject: "True enough.

sentences.zh: 撫寧荒餘，彌成不易。

translations.literal: To calm and nurture the wasted land is all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: To soothe the ravaged provinces is harder still.

sentences.zh: 」榮見四方無事，奏稱「參軍許周勸臣取九錫，臣惡其言，已斥遣令去。

translations.literal: Rong, seeing the four quarters at peace, memorialized: "Adjutant Xu Zhou urged your servant to accept the Nine Bestowals. Your servant detested his words and has dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, seeing the empire quiet, memorialized: "Adjutant Xu Zhou urged me to take the Nine Bestowals. I loathed the suggestion and have sent him away.

sentences.zh: 」榮時望得殊禮，故以意諷朝廷。

translations.literal: Rong at the time hoped for extraordinary honors and thus used the memorial to hint at the court.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was angling for extraordinary honors and used the memorial to needle the court.

sentences.zh: 帝實不欲與之，因稱歎其忠。

translations.literal: The emperor truly did not wish to grant them, but praised Rong's loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no wish to grant them, yet praised Rong's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 榮好獵，不捨寒暑，列圍而進，令士卒必齊壹，雖遇險阻，不得違避，一鹿逸出，必數人坐死。

translations.literal: Rong loved the hunt and never spared himself summer or winter. He drew up encirclements and advanced, ordering the soldiers to keep perfect formation; though they met obstacles, they might not dodge aside. If one deer escaped, several men would be punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong loved the hunt in every season. He ringed the game and drove forward, demanding perfect order from his men; they might not skirt rough ground. If a single deer broke out, several soldiers paid with their lives.

sentences.zh: 有一卒見虎而走，榮謂曰：「汝畏死邪！

translations.literal: One soldier, seeing a tiger, fled. Rong said, "Do you fear death?
translations.idiomatic: One soldier fled at the sight of a tiger. Rong said, "Are you afraid to die?

sentences.zh: 」即斬之。

translations.literal: He was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自是每獵，士卒如登戰場。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever they hunted, the soldiers were as if on a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every hunt felt like a battle.

sentences.zh: 嘗見虎在窮谷中，榮令十餘人空手搏之，毋得損傷。

translations.literal: Once he saw a tiger in a narrow valley. Rong ordered a dozen men to grapple it barehanded without injury.
translations.idiomatic: Once he cornered a tiger in a ravine and ordered a dozen men to wrestle it barehanded without harming it.

sentences.zh: 死者數人，卒擒得之，以此為樂，其下甚苦之。

translations.literal: Several died, but at last they seized it. He took this for sport; his subordinates suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Several died before they took it. Rong called it sport; his men were wretched.

sentences.zh: 太宰天穆從容謂榮曰：「大王勳業已盛，四方無事，唯宜修政養民，順時搜狩，何必盛夏馳逐，感傷和氣？

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Tianmu spoke calmly to Rong: "Your Highness's merit is already great and the four quarters are at peace. You should only cultivate government and nourish the people, and hunt in season—why must you gallop through the height of summer, harming the harmonious qi?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Tianmu said gently, "Your Highness's merit is vast and the realm is at peace. You should govern well and nourish the people, hunting only in season—why race through midsummer and upset heaven's harmony?

sentences.zh: 」榮攘袂曰：「靈後女主，不能自正，推奉天子，乃人臣常節。

translations.literal: Rong flung back his sleeve: "The spirit Empress was a woman who could not keep herself right; to support and serve the Son of Heaven is the constant duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Rong flung back his sleeve. "Empress Ling was a woman who could not govern herself; to raise up and serve the Son of Heaven is what subjects do.

sentences.zh: 葛榮之徒，本皆奴才，乘時作亂，譬如奴走，擒獲即已。

translations.literal: Men like Ge Rong were originally slaves who seized the moment to make trouble—like a runaway slave, once captured it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ge Rong were slaves who seized their moment—like a runaway bondman, once caught, that was the end.

sentences.zh: 頃來受國大恩，未能混壹海內，何得遽言勳業！

translations.literal: Recently we received the state's great favor and have not yet unified all within the seas—how can we speak hastily of merit!
translations.idiomatic: We have only lately received the state's great grace and have not yet united the seas—how dare we speak of finished merit!

sentences.zh: 如聞朝士猶自寬縱，今秋欲與兄戒勒士馬，校獵嵩高，令貪污朝貴，入圍搏虎。

translations.literal: I hear court gentlemen are still lax and indulgent. This autumn I wish to drill troops with my elder brother and hold a great hunt at Song Mountain, forcing corrupt court nobles into the ring to wrestle tigers.
translations.idiomatic: I hear courtiers are still soft and indulgent. This autumn I mean to drill troops with my brother and hunt at Song Mountain, driving corrupt nobles into the ring to fight tigers.

sentences.zh: 仍出魯陽，歷三荊，悉擁生蠻，北填六鎮，回軍之際，掃平汾胡。

translations.literal: Then we shall march out through Luyang, pass through the Three Jing regions, gather all the barbarians, fill the Six Garrisons to the north, and on the return sweep the Fen barbarians clean.
translations.idiomatic: Then we march through Luyang, cross the Three Jing, gather every barbarian band, garrison the Six Frontier Forts to the north, and on the return sweep the Fen River tribes away.

sentences.zh: 明年，簡練精騎，分出江、淮，蕭衍若降，乞萬戶侯；

translations.literal: Next year we shall train elite cavalry and send them out through the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan surrenders, I ask only for a marquisate of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Next year we train elite cavalry and strike south through the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan yields, I ask only for a ten-thousand-household marquisate;

sentences.zh: 如其不降，以數千騎徑度縛取。

translations.literal: if he does not surrender, a few thousand horsemen will cross at a stretch and take him bound.
translations.idiomatic: if not, a few thousand horsemen will cross in a rush and bind him.

sentences.zh: 然後與兄奉天子，巡四方，乃可稱勳耳。

translations.literal: Only then, with my brother escorting the Son of Heaven on a tour of the four quarters, may we call it merit!
translations.idiomatic: Only then, when my brother and I escort the Son of Heaven on a tour of the realm, may we speak of true merit!

sentences.zh: 今不頻獵，兵士懈怠，安可復用也！

translations.literal: If we do not hunt often, the soldiers grow slack—how can they be used again!
translations.idiomatic: Stop hunting and the troops go slack—how then can they be used!

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽之妃，帝之舅女；

translations.literal: The consort of Prince of Chengyang Hui was the emperor's cousin by marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Hui's consort was the emperor's cousin by marriage;

sentences.zh: 侍中李彧，延寔之子，帝之姊婿也。

translations.literal: Master of Ceremonies Li Yu, son of Yanshi, was the emperor's sister's husband.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Ceremonies Li Yu, son of Yanshi, had married the emperor's sister.

sentences.zh: 徽、彧欲得權寵，惡榮為己害，日毀榮於帝，勸帝除之。

translations.literal: Hui and Yu wished for favor and power; they hated Rong as an obstacle to themselves and daily slandered Rong to the emperor, urging him to eliminate Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Yu hungered for favor; they saw Rong as their obstacle and daily poisoned the emperor's ear against him, urging his death.

sentences.zh: 帝懲河陰之難，恐榮終難保，由是密有圖榮之意。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of the disaster at Heyin, feared Rong could not be kept safe in the end; from this he secretly harbored a design against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the massacre at Heyin, the emperor feared Rong could never be kept loyal; secretly he began to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 侍中楊侃、尚書右僕射元羅亦預其謀。

translations.literal: Master of Ceremonies Yang Kan and Right Vice Director Yuan Luo also shared in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Ceremonies Yang Kan and Right Vice Director Yuan Luo joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 會榮請入朝，欲視皇后娩乳。

translations.literal: It happened that Rong asked to enter court, wishing to see the empress nursing her newborn.
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked to enter court, claiming he wished to see the empress nurse her newborn.

sentences.zh: 徽等勸帝因其入，刺殺之。

translations.literal: Hui and the others urged the emperor to take advantage of his entry to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the others urged the emperor to strike when Rong entered.

sentences.zh: 唯膠東侯李侃晞、濟陰王暉業言：「榮若來，必當有備，恐不可圖。

translations.literal: Only Marquis of Jiaodong Li Kanxi and Prince of Jiyin Huiye said, "If Rong comes, he will certainly be on his guard—it may not be possible to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Marquis of Jiaodong Li Kanxi and Prince of Jiyin Huiye objected: "If Rong comes, he will be on guard—the plot may fail.

sentences.zh: 」又欲殺其黨與，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: They also wished to kill his partisans and raise troops to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: They also urged killing his partisans and raising troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 帝疑未定，而洛陽人懷憂懼，中書侍郎邢子才之徒巳避之東出。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and had not decided, while the people of Luoyang were filled with fear; Masters of Writing Xing Zicai and others had already fled eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered. Luoyang was gripped by fear; Masters of Writing Xing Zicai and others had already fled east.

sentences.zh: 榮乃遍與朝士書，相任去留。

translations.literal: Rong then sent letters to all court gentlemen, leaving each free to go or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wrote to every courtier, telling each to stay or go as he chose.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人溫子升以書呈帝，帝恆望其不來，及見書，以榮必來，色甚不悅。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Wen Zisheng presented the letter to the emperor. The emperor had long hoped Rong would not come; when he saw the letter he knew Rong would certainly come and looked deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Wen Zisheng brought the letter to the emperor, who had long prayed Rong would stay away. Seeing it, he knew Rong would come—and his face darkened.

sentences.zh: 子才名邵，以字行，巒之族弟也。

translations.literal: Zicai's given name was Shao; he was known by his courtesy name—a younger cousin of Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai's given name was Shao; he went by his courtesy name, and was a younger cousin of Luan.

sentences.zh: 時人多以字行者，舊史皆因之。

translations.literal: Many at the time were known by their courtesy names; the old historians all follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Many men of the time were known by their courtesy names; older histories follow the same practice.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍奚毅，建義初往來通命，帝每期之甚重，然猶以榮所親信，不敢與之言情。

translations.literal: Martial Guards General Xi Yi, in the Jianyi era, had gone back and forth bearing orders. The emperor had always set great store by him, yet still did not dare confide because Yi was trusted by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guards General Xi Yi had carried messages back and forth since the Jianyi uprising. The emperor valued him deeply, yet dared not confide—Yi was Rong's man.

sentences.zh: 毅曰：「若必有變，臣寧死陛下，不能事契胡！

translations.literal: Yi said, "If there must indeed be a change, your servant would rather die for Your Majesty than serve the Qi-hu!
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "If trouble comes, I would rather die for Your Majesty than serve those barbarians!

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕保天柱無異心，亦不忘卿忠款。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I trust that Heaven's Pillar has no disloyal heart, and I do not forget your loyal candor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I trust Heaven's Pillar is loyal, and I do not forget your devotion.

sentences.zh: 爾朱世隆疑帝欲為變，乃為匿名書自榜其門云：「天子與楊侃、高道穆等為計，欲殺天柱。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong suspected the emperor meant to make a move, and posted an anonymous letter on his own gate: "The Son of Heaven is plotting with Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others to kill Heaven's Pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong suspected the emperor of plotting and posted an anonymous placard on his own gate: "The Son of Heaven, with Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others, plans to kill Heaven's Pillar.

sentences.zh: 」取以呈榮。

translations.literal: He took it and showed it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He took it to Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮自恃其強，不以為意，手毀其書，唾地曰：「世隆無膽。

translations.literal: Rong, relying on his strength, paid no heed, tore the letter with his hand, spat on the ground, and said, "Shilong has no nerve.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, trusting his power, paid no heed. He tore the letter, spat, and said, "Shilong has no stomach for this.

sentences.zh: 誰敢生心！

translations.literal: Who would dare harbor such a thought!
translations.idiomatic: Who would dare raise a hand against me!

sentences.zh: 」榮妻北鄉長公主亦勸榮不行，榮不從。

translations.literal: Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang, also urged Rong not to go; Rong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang, also begged him not to go. Rong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 是月，榮將四五千騎發并州，時人皆言榮反，又云「天子必當圖榮」。

translations.literal: That month Rong set out from Bingzhou with four or five thousand horsemen. People said Rong was rebelling, and also said "The Son of Heaven will surely plot against Rong."
translations.idiomatic: That month Rong left Bingzhou with four or five thousand horsemen. Some said Rong was rebelling; others said, "The emperor will surely move against Rong."

sentences.zh: 九月，榮至洛陽，帝即欲殺之，以太宰天穆在并州，恐為後患，故忍未發，並召天穆。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Rong reached Luoyang. The emperor at once wished to kill him, but because Grand Preceptor Tianmu was in Bingzhou he feared future trouble, so he held back and also summoned Tianmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Rong reached Luoyang. The emperor wanted him dead at once, but Tianmu was still in Bingzhou and might become a threat—so he waited and summoned Tianmu as well.

sentences.zh: 有人告榮云「帝欲圖之。

translations.literal: Someone informed Rong: "The Son of Heaven intends to scheme against you."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Rong: "The emperor means to kill you."

sentences.zh: 」榮即具奏，帝曰：「外人亦言王欲害我，豈可信之！

translations.literal: Rong immediately memorialized in full. The emperor said, "Outsiders also say Your Highness wishes to harm me—how can that be believed!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong memorialized at once. The emperor said, "Outsiders say you mean to harm me—how can I believe that!"

sentences.zh: 」於是榮不自疑，每入謁帝，從人不過數十，又皆挺身不持兵仗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rong no longer suspected; each time he entered to attend the emperor he brought no more than several dozen followers, and all went unarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's suspicions vanished. Each visit he brought only a few dozen followers, all unarmed.

sentences.zh: 帝欲止，城陽王徽曰：「縱不反，亦何可耐！

translations.literal: The emperor wished to stop, but Prince of Chengyang Hui said, "Even if he does not rebel, how can we endure him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated. Prince of Chengyang Hui said, "Even if he is not rebelling, how can we bear him!

sentences.zh: 況不可保邪！

translations.literal: And if he cannot be trusted—how much more!"
translations.idiomatic: And if he cannot be trusted—how much worse!"

sentences.zh: 先是，長星出中台，掃大角；

translations.literal: Earlier, a long-tailed star had appeared in the Central Palace and swept through Great Horn;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a comet had crossed the Central Palace and swept Great Horn;

sentences.zh: 恆州人高榮祖頗知天文，榮問之，對曰：「除舊布新之象也。

translations.literal: Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou knew astronomy rather well. Rong asked him; he answered, "It is the omen of casting off the old and spreading the new."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rongzu of Hengzhou knew the stars. Rong asked him; he said, "It is the sign of casting off the old and raising the new."

sentences.zh: 」榮甚悅。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 榮至洛陽，行台郎中李顯和曰：「天柱至，那無九錫，安須王自索也！

translations.literal: When Rong reached Luoyang, Bureau Director Li Xianhe said, "When Heaven's Pillar arrives, how can there fail to be the Nine Bestowals—why need the king ask for them himself!
translations.idiomatic: When Rong reached Luoyang, Bureau Director Li Xianhe said, "Heaven's Pillar is here—how can the Nine Bestowals be withheld? Why should the king have to ask!

sentences.zh: 亦是天子不見機。

translations.literal: It is also that the Son of Heaven does not read the signs.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven simply cannot read the signs.

sentences.zh: 」都督郭羅剎曰：「今年真可作禪文，何但九錫！

translations.literal: Commander Guo Luosha said, "This year we might truly draft an abdication document—why only the Nine Bestowals!"
translations.idiomatic: Commander Guo Luosha said, "This year we could draft the abdication edict itself—why stop at the Nine Bestowals!"

sentences.zh: 」參軍褚光曰：「人言并州城上有紫氣，何慮天柱不應之！

translations.literal: Adjutant Chu Guang said, "People say purple qi rises above the walls of Bingzhou—why worry that Heaven's Pillar will not answer it!"
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Chu Guang said, "They say purple vapor crowns the walls of Bingzhou—why doubt Heaven's Pillar will answer it!"

sentences.zh: 」榮下人皆陵侮帝左右，無所忌憚，故其事皆上聞。

translations.literal: All those beneath Rong insulted the emperor's attendants without restraint, so everything reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's men insulted the emperor's attendants without fear, and every word reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 奚毅又見帝，求間，帝即下明光殿與語。

translations.literal: Xi Yi saw the emperor again and asked for a private audience. The emperor descended the Bright Hall to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yi sought another audience. The emperor came down from Bright Hall to speak with him alone.

sentences.zh: 知其至誠，乃召城陽王徽及楊侃、李彧，告以毅語。

translations.literal: Knowing Yi's utmost sincerity, he summoned Prince of Chengyang Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu, and told them Yi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced of Yi's loyalty, he summoned Hui, Yang Kan, and Li Yu and repeated what Yi had said.

sentences.zh: 榮小女適帝兄子陳留王寬，榮嘗指之曰：「我終當得此婿力。

translations.literal: Rong's younger daughter had married the emperor's elder brother's son, Prince of Chenliu Kuan. Rong once pointed to him and said, "In the end I shall have the strength of this son-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger daughter had married Prince of Chenliu Kuan, the emperor's nephew. Rong once pointed at him and said, "In the end I will have this son-in-law's strength."

sentences.zh: 」徽以白帝，曰：「榮慮陛下終為己患，脫有東宮，必貪立孩幼，若皇后不生太子，則立陳留耳。

translations.literal: Hui reported to the emperor: "Rong fears Your Majesty will ultimately be his calamity. If there is a crown prince he will surely be eager to set up a child. If the empress does not bear a heir, he will install Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: Hui told the emperor, "Rong fears you will become his enemy. If there is a crown prince he will push a child onto the throne; if the empress bears no son, he will set up Chenliu."

sentences.zh: 」帝夢手持刀自割落十指，惡之，告徽及楊侃。

translations.literal: The emperor dreamed he held a knife and cut off his own ten fingers; he found it ominous and told Hui and Yang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dreamed he cut off his own ten fingers with a knife—a bad omen. He told Hui and Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「蝮蛇螫手，壯士解腕。

translations.literal: Hui said, "When a viper bites the hand, a stalwart man cuts off his wrist.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "When a viper bites the hand, a brave man severs his wrist.

sentences.zh: 割指亦是其類，乃吉祥也。

translations.literal: To cut a finger is of the same kind—it is an auspicious sign."
translations.idiomatic: To lose a finger is the same kind of thing—it is a lucky sign."

sentences.zh: 戊子，天穆至洛陽，帝出迎之。

translations.literal: On day wuzi Tianmu reached Luoyang; the emperor went out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Tianmu reached Luoyang; the emperor went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 榮與天穆並從入西林園宴射，榮奏曰：「近來侍官皆不習武，陛下宜將五百騎出獵，因省辭訟。

translations.literal: Rong and Tianmu together followed in and entered the Western Grove for a feast and archery. Rong memorialized: "Recently the attendant officials have all neglected military arts. Your Majesty should lead five hundred horsemen out to hunt and thereby review lawsuits."
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Tianmu followed him into the Western Grove for feast and archery. Rong said, "Court attendants have grown soft. Your Majesty should take five hundred horsemen hunting and hear lawsuits on the way."

sentences.zh: 」先是，奚毅言榮欲因獵挾天子移都，由是帝益疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier Xi Yi had said Rong wished to use the hunt to seize the Son of Heaven and move the capital; the emperor therefore grew still more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yi had already warned that Rong meant to seize the emperor on the hunt and move the capital—the emperor's suspicion deepened.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝召中書舍人溫子升，告以殺榮狀，並問以殺董卓事，子升具通本末。

translations.literal: On day xinmao the emperor summoned Master of Writing Wen Zisheng, told him of the plan to kill Rong, and asked about the killing of Dong Zhuo. Zisheng laid out the whole story from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the emperor summoned Wen Zisheng, told him the plan to kill Rong, and asked about Dong Zhuo's end. Zisheng recounted the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王允若即赦涼州人，必不應至此。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Had Wang Yun at once pardoned the men of Liangzhou, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If Wang Yun had pardoned the Liangzhou men at once, it would never have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」良久，語子升曰：「朕之情理，卿所具知。

translations.literal: After a long while he said to Zisheng: "My state of mind is something you know full well.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence he told Zisheng, "You know what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 死猶須為，況不必死！

translations.literal: One must act even if death is certain—how much more when death is not certain!
translations.idiomatic: I must act even if death is certain—how much more when it is not!

sentences.zh: 吾寧為高貴鄉公死，不為常道鄉公生！

translations.literal: I would rather die like the Duke of Gaogui than live like the Duke of Changdao!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die like Duke Gaogui than live like Duke Changdao!"

sentences.zh: 」帝謂殺榮、天穆，即赦其黨，皆應不動。

translations.literal: The emperor thought that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their partisans pardoned at once, all would remain still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed that if Rong and Tianmu were killed and their followers pardoned at once, the rest would not stir.

sentences.zh: 應詔王道習曰：「爾朱世隆、司馬子如、朱元龍特為榮所委任，具知天下虛實，謂不宜留。

translations.literal: Master of Documents Wang Daoxi said, "Erzhu Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong are specially entrusted by Rong and know the empire's strengths and weaknesses in full—they should not be left alive."
translations.idiomatic: Master of Documents Wang Daoxi said, "Erzhu Shilong, Sima Ziru, and Zhu Yuanlong are Rong's chosen men and know the realm inside out—they must not be spared."

sentences.zh: 」徽及楊侃皆曰：「若世隆不全，仲遠、天光豈有來理！

translations.literal: Hui and Yang Kan both said, "If Shilong is not eliminated whole, how could Zhongyuan and Tianguang have any reason to come!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Yang Kan said, "If Shilong is not destroyed outright, why would Zhongyuan and Tianguang ever come south!"

sentences.zh: 」帝亦以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor also thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「榮腰間常有刀，或能狼戾傷人，臨事願陛下起避之。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Rong usually carries a knife at his belt and might violently wound someone. At the crisis I beg Your Majesty to rise and avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Rong always wears a knife. He may turn violent—when the moment comes, rise and keep clear of him."

sentences.zh: 」乃伏侃等十餘人於明光殿東。

translations.literal: They then hid Kan and more than ten others east of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: They hid Kan and a dozen others east of Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 其日，榮與天穆並入，坐食未訖，起出，侃等從東階上殿，見榮、天穆已至中庭，事不果。

translations.literal: That day Rong and Tianmu both entered. Before they had finished eating they rose to leave. Kan and the others ascended by the eastern steps; they saw Rong and Tianmu had already reached the central courtyard—the affair came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: That day Rong and Tianmu came in. Before the meal was done they rose to leave. Kan and the others rushed up the eastern steps—but Rong and Tianmu were already in the courtyard. The plot failed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，帝忌曰；

translations.literal: On day renchen—the emperor's day of mourning;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen—the emperor's mourning day;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，榮忌日。

translations.literal: on guisi, Rong's day of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi, Rong's mourning day.

sentences.zh: 甲午，榮暫入，即詣陳留王家飲灑，極醉，遂言病動，頻日不入。

translations.literal: On jiawu Rong entered briefly, then went straight to Prince of Chenliu's house to drink and feast, became utterly drunk, and said illness had come on him; for several days he did not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Rong entered briefly, then went to Prince of Chenliu's house to drink, got roaring drunk, pleaded illness, and stayed away from court for days.

sentences.zh: 帝謀頗洩，世隆又以告榮，且勸其速發。

translations.literal: The emperor's plan leaked rather widely; Shilong again informed Rong and urged him to act quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked. Shilong warned Rong again and urged him to strike quickly.

sentences.zh: 榮輕帝，以為無能為，曰：「何匆匆！

translations.literal: Rong looked down on the emperor, thinking him incapable of action, and said, "What is all this hurry!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong despised the emperor as helpless and said, "What is all this rush!"

sentences.zh: 預帝謀者皆懼，帝患之。

translations.literal: All who shared in the emperor's plot were afraid; the emperor was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the plot was terrified; the emperor was vexed.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽曰：「以生太子為辭，榮必入朝，因此斃之。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui said, "Using the birth of a crown prince as the excuse, Rong will surely enter court—slay him then."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Hui said, "Announce the birth of a crown prince—Rong will surely come to court. Kill him then."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「後懷孕始九月，可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The empress has been pregnant only nine months—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The empress is only nine months gone—will that convince him?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「婦人不及期而產者多矣，彼必不疑。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Women often give birth before term—they will surely not suspect."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Women often deliver early—they will never suspect."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝伏兵於明光殿東序，聲言皇子生，遣徽馳騎至榮第告之。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, the Emperor hid soldiers in the eastern gallery of Mingguang Hall, proclaimed that the prince was born, and sent Wei by swift horse to Rong's residence to tell him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor hid troops in the eastern gallery of Mingguang Hall, announced the prince's birth, and sent Wei galloping to Rong's mansion with the news.

sentences.zh: 榮方與上黨王天穆博，徽脫榮帽，歡舞盤旋，兼殿內文武傳聲趣之，榮遂信之，與天穆俱入朝。

translations.literal: Rong was just gambling with Prince of Shangdang Tianmu. Wei snatched off Rong's cap and danced and whirled about; within the hall civil and military officials all passed word urging him on. Rong therefore believed it and entered court with Tianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was gambling with Prince of Shangdang Tianmu. Wei snatched off his cap and danced for joy while courtiers shouted the summons. Rong believed them and entered with Tianmu.

sentences.zh: 帝聞榮來，不覺失色，中書舍人溫子升曰：「陛下色變。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard Rong was coming, he could not help changing color. Secretariat Cadet Wen Zisheng said, "Your Majesty's color has changed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Rong was coming, the emperor went pale. Wen Zisheng murmured, "Your Majesty—you have turned color.

sentences.zh: 」帝連索酒飲之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor repeatedly called for wine and drank.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor called for wine again and again and drank.

sentences.zh: 帝令子升作赦文，既成，執以出，遇榮自外入，問：「是何文書？

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zisheng to draft an amnesty. When it was done, he took it and went out and met Rong entering from outside. Rong asked, "What document is that?
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zisheng to draft an amnesty. Zisheng came out with it just as Rong entered and asked, "What is that paper?

sentences.zh: 」子升顏色不變，曰：「敕。

translations.literal: " Zisheng's expression did not change. He said, "An edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Zisheng never flinched. "An edict.

sentences.zh: 」榮不取視而入。

translations.literal: " Rong did not take it to look and entered.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong did not look and passed inside.

sentences.zh: 帝在東序下西向坐，榮、天穆在御榻西北南向坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor sat below the eastern gallery facing west. Rong and Tianmu sat northwest of the imperial couch facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat in the eastern gallery facing west. Rong and Tianmu sat northwest of the couch, facing south.

sentences.zh: 徽入，始一拜，榮見光祿少卿魯安、典御李侃晞等抽刀從東戶入，即起趨御座。

translations.literal: Wei entered and had just made one bow when Rong saw Director of the Imperial Banquets Lu An, Palace Steward Li Kanxi, and others draw swords and enter from the eastern door. He at once rose and rushed toward the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei entered and bowed once. Rong saw Lu An, Li Kanxi, and others burst in from the east door with swords drawn and sprang for the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝先橫刀膝下，遂手刃之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already laid a knife across his knees and thereupon stabbed Rong with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already had a knife across his knees and drove it into Rong himself.

sentences.zh: 安等亂斫，榮與天穆同時俱死。

translations.literal: An and the others hacked wildly. Rong and Tianmu died at the same moment.
translations.idiomatic: An and the rest cut them down. Rong and Tianmu fell together.

sentences.zh: 榮子菩提及車騎將軍爾朱陽睹等三十人從榮入宮，亦為伏兵所殺。

translations.literal: Rong's son Puti and Cavalry General Erzhu Yangdu and thirty others who had followed Rong into the palace were also killed by the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's son Puti, Cavalry General Erzhu Yangdu, and thirty who had followed him inside were cut down by the ambush.

sentences.zh: 帝得榮手板，上有數牒啟，皆左右去留人名，非其腹心者悉在出限。

translations.literal: The Emperor obtained Rong's hand board. On it were several memorial slips, all names of men about the sovereign kept or dismissed—those who were not his intimates were all marked for removal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized Rong's hand board. On it were lists of who should stay or go at court—everyone not in Rong's inner circle marked for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豎子若過今日，遂不可制。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Had that brat passed this day, he could never have been controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Had that wretch lived past today, he would never have been mastered.

sentences.zh: 」於是內外喜噪，聲滿洛陽城，百僚入賀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon inside and outside rejoiced with clamor; the sound filled Luoyang city. The hundred officials entered to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: " Inside and outside erupted in joy; the roar filled Luoyang. Officials poured in to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 帝登閶闔門，下詔大赦，遣武衛將軍奚毅、前燕州刺史崔淵將兵鎮北中。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the Changhe Gate, issued an edict of general amnesty, and sent Martial Guards General Xi Yi and former Yanzhou Inspector Cui Yuan with troops to hold North Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the Changhe Gate, proclaimed amnesty, and sent Xi Yi and former Yanzhou inspector Cui Yuan to hold North Zhong.

sentences.zh: 是夜，爾朱世隆奉北鄉長公主帥榮部曲，焚西陽門，出屯河陰。

translations.literal: That night, Erzhu Shilong, escorting the Northern Country Princess, led Rong's troops, burned the Xiyang Gate, and went out to camp at River Yin.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shilong, with the Northern Country Princess, led Rong's troops, burned the Xiyang Gate, and encamped at River Yin.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍賀拔勝與榮黨田怡等聞榮死。

translations.literal: Guards General Heba Sheng and Rong's partisan Tian Yi and others heard Rong was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Guards General Heba Sheng and Rong's men Tian Yi and others heard Rong was dead.

sentences.zh: 奔赴榮第。

translations.literal: They rushed to Rong's residence.
translations.idiomatic: They galloped to Rong's mansion.

sentences.zh: 時宮殿門猶未加嚴防，怡等議即攻門，勝止之曰：「天子既行大事，必當有備，吾等眾少，何可輕爾！

translations.literal: At the time the palace gates were not yet under strict guard. Yi and the others discussed attacking the gate at once. Sheng stopped them and said, "The Son of Heaven has already done a great deed and will surely be prepared. We are few—how can we act rashly!
translations.idiomatic: The palace gates were not yet sealed. Yi urged an immediate assault. Sheng stopped him: "The emperor has struck and will be ready. We are too few—this is folly!

sentences.zh: 但得出城，更為它計。

translations.literal: We need only get out of the city and plan something else.
translations.idiomatic: Get out of the city first, then choose another course.

sentences.zh: 」怡乃止。

translations.literal: " Yi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi desisted.

sentences.zh: 及世隆走，勝遂不從，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Shilong fled, Sheng would not follow; the Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong fled, Sheng refused to join him, and the emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 朱瑞雖為榮所委，而善處朝廷之間，帝亦善遇之，故瑞從世隆走而中道逃還。

translations.literal: Zhu Rui, though entrusted by Rong, was skilled in managing relations with the court, and the Emperor also treated him well. Therefore Rui fled with Shilong but turned back midway.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rui, though Rong's man, had always navigated the court well and the emperor favored him; he left with Shilong but turned back halfway.

sentences.zh: 榮素厚金紫光祿大夫司馬子如，榮死，子如自宮中突出，至榮第，棄家，隨榮妻子走出城。

translations.literal: Rong had long favored Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Sima Ziru. When Rong died, Ziru burst out of the palace, reached Rong's residence, abandoned his household, and followed Rong's wife and children out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had favored Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Sima Ziru. When Rong fell, Ziru bolted from the palace to Rong's house, abandoned his family, and fled the city with Rong's kin.

sentences.zh: 世隆即欲還北，子如曰：「兵不厭詐，今天下恟恟，唯強是視，當此之際，不可以弱示人。

translations.literal: Shilong at once wished to return north. Ziru said, "In war one does not weary of deceit. Now the empire is in uproar and men look only to strength. At such a moment one must not show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong meant to flee north. Ziru said, "War does not weary of deceit. The realm is in uproar and men worship strength—you must not look weak.

sentences.zh: 若亟北走，恐變生肘腋。

translations.literal: If we hurry north, I fear trouble will arise at our elbows.
translations.idiomatic: Race north and trouble will spring up at your elbow.

sentences.zh: 不如分兵守河橋，還軍向京師，出其不意，或可成功。

translations.literal: Better to divide troops to hold the River Bridge, turn the army back on the capital, and take them unawares—perhaps we may succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Better hold the River Bridge, wheel on the capital, and strike by surprise—you may yet win.

sentences.zh: 假使不得所欲，亦足示有餘力，使天下畏我之強，不敢叛散。

translations.literal: Even if we do not get what we desire, it is enough to show we still have strength, make the empire fear our power, and dare not rebel and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you fail, you will show you still have force, frighten the realm, and keep men from scattering.

sentences.zh: 」世隆從之。

translations.literal: " Shilong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilong agreed.

sentences.zh: 己亥，攻河橋，擒奚毅等，殺之，據北中城。

translations.literal: On day jihai, they attacked the River Bridge, captured Xi Yi and others, killed them, and held North Zhong city.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they stormed the River Bridge, seized Xi Yi and others, executed them, and held North Zhong.

sentences.zh: 魏朝大懼，遣前華陽太守段育慰諭之，世隆斬首以徇。

translations.literal: The Wei court was greatly afraid and sent former Huayang Administrator Duan Yu to reassure them. Shilong beheaded him and displayed the head.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court, terrified, sent former Huayang administrator Duan Yu to parley. Shilong beheaded him and displayed the head.

sentences.zh: 魏以雍州刺史爾朱天光為侍中、儀同三司，以司空楊津為都督並、肆等九州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、并州刺史，兼尚書令、北道大行台，經略河、汾。

translations.literal: Wei made Yongzhou Inspector Erzhu Tianguang Palace Attendant and Holder of the Same Rank as the Three Dukes, and made Minister of Works Yang Jin Commander-in-Chief of the nine provinces Bing, Xi, and others, Cavalry General-in-Chief, Inspector of Bingzhou, and concurrently Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Northern Route Grand Commissioner, to manage the He and Fen rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Yongzhou inspector Erzhu Tianguang palace attendant with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, and Yang Jin minister of works, commander of Bing, Xi, and seven other provinces, cavalry general-in-chief, Bingzhou inspector, concurrent minister of state, and northern-route grand commissioner over the He and Fen.

sentences.zh: 榮之入洛也，以高敖曹自隨，禁於駝牛署。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, he had brought Gao Aocao with him and confined him at the Camel-Ox Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang he had brought Gao Aocao and held him at the Camel-Ox Office.

sentences.zh: 榮死，帝引見，勞勉之。

translations.literal: When Rong died, the Emperor summoned and received him, consoled and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death the emperor received him, consoled him, and praised him.

sentences.zh: 兄乾自東冀州馳赴洛陽，帝以乾為河北大使，敖曹為直閣將軍，使歸，招集鄉曲為表裡形援。

translations.literal: His elder brother Gan galloped from Eastern Jizhou to Luoyang. The Emperor made Gan envoy to Hebei and Aocao Direct Attendant, sent them back to gather their home districts as inner and outer support.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Gan raced from Eastern Jizhou to Luoyang. The emperor made Gan Hebei envoy and Aocao direct attendant and sent them home to rally their countrymen as a reserve force.

sentences.zh: 帝親送之於河橋，舉酒指水曰：「卿兄弟冀部豪傑，能令士卒致死，京城倘有變，可為朕河上一揚塵。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally saw them off at the River Bridge, raised his cup and pointed at the water, saying, "You brothers are heroes of Jizhou. If you can make your soldiers die for you, should the capital meet with trouble, you may raise a dust for me on the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the River Bridge the emperor saw them off, cup in hand, and pointed at the water: "You are heroes of Ji. If you can make men die for you, raise dust on this river for me should the capital falter.

sentences.zh: 」乾垂涕受詔，敖曹援劍起舞，誓以必死。

translations.literal: " Gan received the command with tears. Aocao seized his sword and danced, vowing to die without fail.
translations.idiomatic: " Gan wept as he accepted. Aocao drew his sword, danced, and swore to die.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸卯朔，世隆遣爾朱拂律歸將胡騎一千，皆白服，來至郭下，索太原王屍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day guimao, Shilong sent Erzhu Fulügui to lead a thousand Hu horse, all in white dress, to the suburbs, demanding the corpse of the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, first day guimao: Shilong sent Erzhu Fulügui with a thousand Hu cavalry in white to the suburbs, demanding the Prince of Taiyuan's body.

sentences.zh: 帝升大夏門望之，遣主書牛法尚謂之曰：「太原王立功不終，陰圖釁逆，王法無親，已正刑書。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the Daxia Gate to look at them and sent Chief Clerk Niu Fashang to say, "The Prince of Taiyuan's merit was not carried through to the end; he secretly plotted sedition. The king's law knows no kin—the sentence is already executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the Daxia Gate and sent Chief Clerk Niu Fashang: "The Prince of Taiyuan's merit went unfinished; he plotted treason. The law knows no kin—the sentence stands.

sentences.zh: 罪止榮身，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: Guilt stops with Rong's person; the rest are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt ends with Rong alone; the rest are untouched.

sentences.zh: 卿等若降，官爵如故。

translations.literal: If you submit, offices and ranks are as before.
translations.idiomatic: Submit and your offices remain.

sentences.zh: 」拂律歸曰：「臣等從太原王入朝，忽致冤酷，今不忍空歸。

translations.literal: " Fulügui said, "We followed the Prince of Taiyuan into court and suddenly met cruel injustice. Now we cannot bear to return empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: " Fulügui said, "We followed the Prince of Taiyuan to court and met butchery. We cannot go home empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 願得太原王屍，生死無恨。

translations.literal: We ask only for the Prince of Taiyuan's corpse—then living or dying we have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Give us his body, and we will live or die content.

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣，哀不自勝，群胡皆慟哭，聲振城邑。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wept; grief mastered him. All the Hu wailed; the sound shook the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept until he could not speak. The Hu wailed together until the city shook.

sentences.zh: 帝亦為之愴然，遣侍中朱瑞繼鐵券賜世隆。

translations.literal: The Emperor also was moved for them and sent Palace Attendant Zhu Rui with an iron certificate to bestow on Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and sent Zhu Rui with an iron certificate for Shilong.

sentences.zh: 世隆謂瑞曰：「太原王功格天地，赤心奉國，長樂不顧信誓，枉加屠害，今日兩行鐵字，何足可信！

translations.literal: Shilong said to Rui, "The Prince of Taiyuan's merit fills heaven and earth; with a loyal heart he served the state. Changle broke faith and slaughtered him unjustly—today two lines of iron, how can they be trusted!
translations.idiomatic: Shilong told Rui, "Taiyuan's merit filled heaven and earth; he served with a loyal heart. Changle broke faith and butchered him—what are two lines of iron worth now?

sentences.zh: 吾為太原王報仇，終無降理！

translations.literal: I avenge the Prince of Taiyuan and will never have reason to surrender!
translations.idiomatic: I avenge Taiyuan—I will never surrender!

sentences.zh: 」瑞還，白帝，帝即出庫物置城西門外，募敢死之士以討世隆，一日即得萬人，與拂律歸等戰於郭外。

translations.literal: " Rui returned and reported to the Emperor. The Emperor at once brought out treasury goods and set them outside the western gate, recruiting dare-to-die men to attack Shilong. In one day he got ten thousand and fought Fulügui and the others outside the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui returned. The emperor opened the treasury outside the western gate, raised ten thousand dare-to-die men in a day, and fought Fulügui outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 拂律歸等生長戎旅，洛陽之人不習戰鬥，屢戰不克。

translations.literal: Fulügui and the others had grown up in the army; the men of Luoyang were unskilled in battle and repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Fulügui's men were born to war; Luoyang's citizens were not. The city troops lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以前車騎大將軍李叔仁為大都督，帥眾討世隆。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, former Cavalry General-in-Chief Li Shuren was made Grand Commander and led the host to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen former cavalry general-in-chief Li Shuren became grand commander and marched against Shilong.

sentences.zh: 戊申，皇子生，大赦。

translations.literal: On day wushen, the prince was born and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the prince was born and amnesty was declared.
